input.reasoning:
Estimated using story points as a proxy for effort, converting points to engineering hours via a standard heuristic (1 point ≈ 6-7 hours of blended engineering effort), then split across roles based on task nature (backend-heavy, frontend-heavy, infra, data-migration, QA-heavy, etc.). Total backlog = 209 points across 24 tasks.

Role allocation logic:
- Backend Developer (1.5 FTE, 98.33/hr): primary owner of API/auth/payment/RBAC/migration/audit/search/multi-currency/rate-limiting work - the largest share of backend-heavy tickets (PW-1,3,4,6,7,8,9,10,11,13,14,17,21,22,23,24 partial).
- Frontend Developer (1.0 FTE, 90/hr): owns UI-heavy tickets (PW-2,3,4,5,6,9,12,13,15,16,18,19,20) plus UI portions of shared tickets.
- QA Engineer (0.6 FTE, 70/hr): testing across all tickets, weighted heavier on Urgent/High priority and payment/migration/security items.
- DevOps Engineer (0.4 FTE, 110/hr): CI/CD (PW-1), observability (PW-22), decommission (PW-24), and infra support for migration/payments.

Capacity check: 1.5 FTE Backend over ~13 weeks (a typical mid-size portal build) = 1.5*40*13 ≈ 780 hrs; we allocated ~760 backend hours, close to full capacity. Frontend 1.0 FTE*40*13=520 hrs, allocated ~430 hrs - leaves buffer for the design-system and accessibility rework. QA 0.6 FTE*40*13=312 hrs, allocated ~230 hrs - reasonable given QA is a shared/support role. DevOps 0.4 FTE*40*13=208 hrs, allocated ~110 hrs - DevOps is thinly staffed and is a scheduling risk flagged as an assumption, especially given CI/CD, migration cutover and payment observability all compete for the same 0.4 FTE.

Non-labour costs: Stripe integration environment/sandbox fees, Oracle migration tooling/consulting buffer, staging/cloud infra during build, and a contingency/PM tooling line.

Priority breakdown computed by summing labour cost per ticket priority group scaled by points share of total effort.

Reductions: three concrete descope/reduction levers are offered - deferring two Low-priority tickets (Usage analytics, Admin back-office) to a later phase, trimming QA hours on Low priority tickets, and deferring the Contract-tests/Decommission legacy portal tickets which have no urgent business driver.

Scenarios: Best case assumes low integration friction and stable scope (~10% below base); Most likely is the base estimate; Worst case adds a contingency for migration/payment integration risk and DevOps bottleneck (~20% above base), consistent with typical software delivery variance and the fact no historical actuals exist for this specific team/client combination.

nonLabourLines.description: Stripe sandbox/production integration & PCI review fees
Legacy Oracle migration tooling & DBA consulting buffer
Cloud infra (staging + prod) during build phase, ~4 months
Contingency / PM & tooling overhead (10% of labour)

assumptions: No historical actuals (real spend data) are available for this project yet; all figures are derived from story points and role-based heuristics, not observed velocity.
1 story point ≈ 6-7 hours of blended engineering effort, informed by typical mid-complexity SaaS portal work.
Backend Developer at 1.5 FTE is allocated ~760 hours against an available ~780 hours over an assumed 13-week build, i.e. near full capacity - this role is the critical bottleneck.

DevOps Engineer is only 0.4 FTE (~208 hrs capacity over 13 weeks) but must cover CI/CD setup, migration cutover support, payment observability and legacy decommission - this role is thinly staffed relative to backlog demand and is flagged as a scheduling risk.

QA Engineer at 0.6 FTE is assumed to test across all tickets but with lighter touch on Low-priority items; dedicated QA hours are weighted toward Urgent/High priority and security/payment-sensitive tickets.
Legacy data migration (PW-8) is assumed to require significant external DBA/tooling support beyond pure engineering hours, captured as a non-labour line rather than additional engineer hours.
Frontend Developer at 1.0 FTE is assumed sufficient for UI-heavy tickets without needing overtime, leaving some schedule buffer for design system rework and accessibility pass iteration.
Estimate assumes no major re-scoping mid-project and a single client-side stakeholder for sign-off; multiple rounds of stakeholder rework are not included.
Priority breakdown costs are approximate allocations of total labour cost proportional to story points within each priority band, not independently re-derived bottom-up estimates.

reductions.description: Defer PW-19 (Usage analytics and reporting) and PW-18 (Admin back-office for support staff) to a post-launch phase 2, since both are Low priority and not required for customer-facing launch.
reductions.effect: Removes ~21 points (roughly 130 backend + 70 frontend hours) from the current phase; re-planned for a later release.

reductions.description: Reduce QA hours allocated to Low-priority tickets (PW-12, PW-18, PW-19, PW-23, PW-24) to smoke-test level rather than full regression coverage.
reductions.effect: Cuts ~80 QA hours across five low-priority tickets; residual risk accepted for non-critical features.

reductions.description: Defer PW-23 (Contract tests against helpdesk API) and PW-24 (Decommission legacy portal) until after the new portal has been live and stable for one release cycle.
reductions.effect: Removes ~13 points of backend/DevOps effort from this phase; legacy portal kept running slightly longer at modest ongoing hosting cost.

reductions.description: Reduce scope of PW-14 (Multi-currency support) to EUR/USD only at launch, adding PLN in a later iteration once real demand is confirmed.
reductions.effect: Cuts roughly one-third of the estimated backend/frontend effort on this ticket by removing one currency and its FX/reconciliation edge cases initially.

reductions.description: Delay non-essential observability tooling spend (APM licence) until closer to go-live rather than provisioning it at project start.
reductions.effect: Removes the APM licence non-labour cost from this phase's budget; added back before production launch.
